findings.bible: 3.2 options table: CNA_TEST_DISPLAY bakes a DISPLAY value into every window-creating ctest's ENVIRONMENT together with SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11; set :99 for Xvfb. Ledger WPB1-arch-051 records the default as ':0' and cites development/testing/index.html#gpu.
findings.target: cmake/TestDisplayPolicy.cmake: CNA_TEST_DISPLAY defaults to empty; a value naming display :0 is honoured only with CNA_TEST_ALLOW_LIVE_DISPLAY=ON and is otherwise reset to empty; other values (for example :99) are honoured; every non-Windows test gets a Wayland guard; the per-test clearing needs CMake >= 3.28 (cmake_language(DEFER DIRECTORY)); older CMake leaves an empty DISPLAY and warns.
findings.site_now: The behaviour is stated correctly on development/takeover/validation.html, development/getting-started.html, docs/verification.html, tutorial 160 and the options reference, but the ledger's destination development/testing/index.html#gpu only mentions that the private wrapper refuses a tree that forces a display; it does not state the CNA_TEST_DISPLAY policy. The ledger concept text (default :0) is stale.

fix.html: Which display a registered test uses is the CNA_TEST_DISPLAY cache value (cmake/TestDisplayPolicy.cmake). It is empty by default, so each window-creating test inherits the caller's DISPLAY; a value naming the live desktop (:0) is honoured only together with CNA_TEST_ALLOW_LIVE_DISPLAY=ON and is otherwise reset to empty; any other value, for example :99 for an Xvfb, is forced into the renderer tests' environment together with SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11. Non-Windows registrations also carry a Wayland guard so an unset WAYLAND_DISPLAY cannot fall back to the live compositor. Clearing the per-test DISPLAY and adding the guard need CMake 3.28 or newer; on older CMake the tests keep an empty DISPLAY and the configure warns. Read at the pinned commit; not executed.

fix.html: Two exceptions are recorded in CHECKLIST.md. A C# internal set becomes a private setter plus friend class <OneSpecificClass> (the Microsoft::Devices::Sensors reading types friend only their own sensor class), which is narrower than C#'s assembly-wide access. And a C# internal const or internal static readonly field that another translation unit genuinely needs is exposed as a CNAEXT public static constexpr, with a note citing the FNA declaration, rather than duplicated or left unreachable: GamePad::LeftDeadZone, RightDeadZone and TriggerThreshold, and TouchPanel::MAX_TOUCHES (8) and NO_FINGER (-1). findings.bible: F68: orientation is derived from bounds, not from a sensor: Portrait iff Height > Width, else LandscapeLeft, Default for non-positive extents; LandscapeRight is never produced by the refresh path, only by SetSupportedOrientations' fallback chain (Game window section). Ledger WPB1-fcm-044 marks it SUPERSEDED ('the bounds-only rule is alpha.1').
findings.target: modules/runtime/src/GameWindow.cpp::refreshCachedPlatformState and ::orientationFromBounds (Height > Width gives Portrait, otherwise LandscapeLeft, non-positive gives Default; the bounds are the logical size when a provider is installed; the result is adopted only if orientationIsSupported) and ::SetSupportedOrientations (fallback order Portrait, LandscapeLeft, LandscapeRight, Default). The bounds rule still holds at TARGET; only its input changed.
findings.site_now: development/internals/runtime/module.html#objects: 'it is portrait when the logical height exceeds the width, landscape otherwise, and is only adopted if it is in the supported set'. It does not name the enumerator (LandscapeLeft), the Default result, or that LandscapeRight is never derived from the shape, so a port that tests CurrentOrientation == LandscapeRight for flipped landscape never sees it. LandscapeRight appears nowhere on the site.

fix.old_html: it is portrait when the logical height exceeds the width, landscape otherwise, and is only adopted if it is in the supported set.
fix.html: it is Portrait when the logical height exceeds the width, LandscapeLeft otherwise and Default when either extent is not positive, and is only adopted if it is in the supported set. LandscapeRight is therefore never derived from the surface shape: CurrentOrientation can become LandscapeRight only through the fallback in SetSupportedOrientations (tried after Portrait and LandscapeLeft), so a port that compares CurrentOrientation with LandscapeRight will not see it after a device rotation. Read at this snapshot; not run on a phone.

findings.bible: F28: Game::Update and Game::Draw snapshot the component list into a member vector, then clear it; add/remove during iteration is safe, but the snapshot is a member, not a local, so a re-entrant Update (a component calling Game::Update) would clobber it; re-entrancy is untested (Components section).
findings.target: modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp::Game::Update and ::Game::Draw clear currentlyUpdatingComponents_/currentlyDrawingComponents_ on entry, fill them under componentListsMutex_, iterate them with a range-based for and clear them on exit; the members are declared in Game.hpp. ::OnComponentRemoved nulls entries in the same vectors. No re-entrancy guard exists and no test under modules/runtime/tests enters Update, Draw or Tick re-entrantly.
findings.site_now: development/internals/runtime/module.html#components explains the snapshot copy under the lock and the null-marking in OnComponentRemoved, but never says the two vectors are members shared by nested calls; no other page mentions it.

fix.old_html: the screen-manager case where the update that is running drops the screen owning the components.
fix.html:
the screen-manager case where the update that is running drops the screen owning the components.

The two snapshot vectors are members of Game, not locals, and each call clears its vector on entry and again on exit. A Game::Update or Game::Draw entered again from inside a component's own Update or Draw (or from a nested loop that calls Tick()) therefore empties and refills the vector the outer loop is still iterating, which invalidates the outer loop's iterators (formally undefined behaviour). Nothing in the runtime guards against it and no runtime test enters the loop re-entrantly. Read from Game.cpp at this snapshot; not executed.

GDI, HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM always throw, and STUB never reaches the path because its draws are no-ops.

The null-object resources are the NoOp* classes in NoOp3DResources.hpp: vertex and index buffers, an occlusion query, a volume texture, a cube texture and a cube render target. They keep only the counts and sizes the public wrappers need, allocate no GPU storage and never draw. The four families that honour WarnAndStub return them from their 3D factories after HandleUnsupported3DCall has logged the warning (a few factories return null instead when the policy is Throw, and the public constructor then refuses). The active policy is read back with GraphicsDevice::GetUnsupported3DGraphicsCallBehavior(). Read at the pinned commit; not executed.
